name: Ironveil Splitback Ghost Operative Rig
description: This is a runner's rig built around a heavy chrome arm and a reputation — it doesn't hide what the wearer is so much as it makes them look like someone you've already decided not to bother. The centerpiece is a structured asymmetric long jacket in deep charcoal with a burgundy-wine underlining visible only at the split hem and rolled cuffs. The right side is a standard close-fit silhouette; the left side has a full external split from hip to shoulder — a split-back panel that opens wide to accommodate a full chrome arm prosthetic, with reinforced mag-seam closures that can be sealed in under two seconds for a cleaner look. The aug-power routing runs exposed along the left lapel in a matte brushed-metal channel — intentional, a design choice that reads as style rather than utility to the untrained eye. Beneath the jacket is a high-neck compression top in deep plum with embedded thermal regulation and a single BCI-relay strip along the spine. The trousers are dark earth-brown slim-taper with reinforced inner thighs, four concealed side-entry pockets, and a hidden calf channel for a compact holdout weapon. Boots are heavy matte black knee-highs in pressure-formed synth-leather with a built-in shin guard layer and concealed blade-channel in the right boot shaft. A pair of matte graphite fingerless gloves with embedded grip pads and scanner-opacity knuckle panels completes the look. This outfit says the runner has a name people know.
materials: charcoal structured ripstop with burgundy-wine lining
functionality: Full-split left panel for chrome arm access with mag-seam rapid-close; exposed aug-power routing channel along left lapel; BCI-relay strip along spine; thermal regulation base layer; four concealed side-entry trouser pockets; hidden calf weapon channel; boot shaft blade channel; scanner-opacity knuckle panels on gloves; knee-high shin guard layer in boots
what_it_says: This runner isn't hiding. They're known — or they want to be. The asymmetric split jacket with the exposed aug-power channel is a statement: I have a chrome arm, I have a rep, and I dressed for this job specifically. It sits at the edge of Tier 3-4 presentation, expensive enough to suggest the work pays well, specific enough to say the wearer has been doing it long enough to develop preferences.
worn_by: runners whose rep is part of the job
manufacturer: Ironveil — street label, Shelf-origin, now Circuit-distributed
story_hooks: The runner's jacket has been flagged in three separate corpsec incident reports under the same description — 'asymmetric charcoal split-back, chrome arm' — and a bounty has been placed not on the person but on the jacket itself, as the only consistent identifier for a runner who changes everything else.

The mag-seam on the left split panel fails mid-extraction, and the runner has to complete a job through a Tier 3 corporate lobby with their chrome arm fully exposed and the jacket hanging open — every camera in the building gets a perfect shot.
A younger runner shows up to a job wearing a near-identical knockoff of the same jacket, which the original wearer takes as either flattery or a calculated provocation.

physical_description.visual_profile: Asymmetric runner's operative rig with dominating left-side chrome arm accommodation. Silhouette reads deliberately unbalanced—right side tailored and clean, left side boldly split and weaponized. Deep charcoal jacket with burgundy wine linings creates visual depth. The exposed aug-power routing along the left lapel reads as intentional chrome-and-fabric fusion. Overall impression: dangerous competence, street-tier reputation, someone who's already made augmentation choices everyone can see.
physical_description.fit: Right side close-fit and structured; left side deliberately loose to accommodate full chrome prosthetic arm. Jacket cuts long and dramatic with high-neck compression top creating a streamlined torso. Trousers slim-taper with reinforced geometry at stress points. Boots knee-high with integrated armor suggestion. Compression layers create a second-skin effect beneath the statement jacket.
physical_description.primary_material: Jacket: ballistic charcoal weave with burgundy synthetic underlining. Compression top: thermal-regulation plum synthetic. Trousers: reinforced dark earth-brown synth-composite. Boots: pressure-formed matte black synth-leather with shin guard laminate. Gloves: graphite-grey synthetic with embedded grip compound.
physical_description.texture: Jacket exterior matte with subtle weave pattern; burgundy linings glossy-smooth. Matte brushed-metal aug-power channel runs tactile and intentional. Compression top has fine ribbed texture. Trousers have reinforced diagonal weave at thighs. Boot leather pressure-formed for urban grip, not glossy. Gloves have textured grip-pad zones on palms and fingers.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep charcoal primary with burgundy-wine accent linings. Plum compression top. Dark earth-brown trousers. Matte black boots. Graphite-grey gloves. Brushed-metal aug-channel adds cool metallic accent. Palette reads urban-nocturnal with hidden wine-colored warmth.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: magnetic snap closures along the split-back panel for rapid seal-up (under 2 seconds). Standard zip closure for main front. Compression top: friction-fit. Trousers: magnetic snap at waist with concealed side-entry pocket access. Boots: pressure-lock friction fit. Gloves: friction-seal wrist bands.

physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 working operative. Street-origin Ironveil label now Circuit-distributed. Price point accessible to serious runners with augmentation investment. Not corpo-tier luxury, but purposeful and equipped.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street operative/runner aesthetic. Wearer has committed to augmentation visibly and isn't hiding it—confidence signal. Military-adjacent utility. Sub-grade survivalist mentality with mid-tier access. Says: 'I've made the augmentation choice, I have a reputation, I know how to move through the city, don't test me.'
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in but maintained. Mag-seams show minor polish wear. Burgundy linings visible from repeated jacket opens. Glove grip pads worn smooth from actual use. Boots scuffed at heel and toe, shin guard showing contact marks. Jacket fabric has lived-in patina, not fresh. Aug-channel shows micro-scratches from daily arm swaps and routing maintenance. Overall: functional veteran gear, not pristine, but religiously maintained.
